title: Smallest Stable Index I
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the smallest index i where the difference between the maximum value in nums[0..i] and the minimum value in nums[i..n-1] is less than or equal to k.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the smallest index i where the difference between the maximum value in nums[0..i] and the minimum value in nums[i..n-1] is less than or equal to k. If no such index exists, return -1.
constraints: At index i, compare the maximum over nums[0..i] with the minimum over nums[i..n-1].
The index is stable when their difference is at most k.
Return the smallest stable index, or -1.
hints: Precompute the minimum of every suffix.
Scan left to right while maintaining the prefix maximum.
Test their difference against k at each index.
Return the first passing index to enforce smallest order.
editorial: Return the first passing index to enforce smallest order.

tests.explanation: Only index three has prefix maximum five and suffix minimum four within distance three.
Index zero has prefix maximum and suffix minimum both one, so return zero.
